notes: Mixed filler, not all long filler like La Aurora's core lines. No strength rating has been published. Sold in bundles, named for Santiago de los Caballeros.

about: The classic Connecticut-wrapped León Jimenes line made by La Aurora in the Dominican Republic. It is a smooth, light cigar that has long sold better abroad than in the U.S.
notes: The maker gives no strength word and its strength gauge reads 65 out of 100, but retailers call it mild. Sizes come from a European retailer, where the line is simply called León Jimenes. Launch year is unclear.
verifyNotes: Added the Belicoso (6.5 x 52), which the cigarworld listing shows as a current size. Notes now mention the maker's strength gauge (65 of 100), which the researcher missed and which conflicts with retailers calling it mild. Softened the about line on where it sells and trimmed notes.

about: A darker, fuller take on León Jimenes from La Aurora, with a Brazilian maduro wrapper and tobacco aged at least three years. It comes in thicker formats than the classic line.
notes: The maker gives no strength word; its strength gauge reads 75 out of 100. The maker lists a Dominican binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler, while one European retailer lists a Brazilian binder and four-country filler. Sizes come from that retailer.
verifyNotes: Blend and sizes confirmed. Notes now give the maker's strength gauge (75 of 100) instead of saying nothing is published, and were trimmed.

about: A León Jimenes blend from La Aurora launched in 2011 to reintroduce the brand in the U.S., originally sold in black and gold tubes. It is a smooth cigar the maker suggests for newer smokers.
notes: The maker calls it mild to medium bodied. The maker's current blend (Ecuadorian binder, three-country filler) differs from halfwheel's 2011 prerelease listing of a Dominican and Nicaraguan binder over Dominican filler. Sizes are the three launch sizes.

about: A León Jimenes line La Aurora created in 2007 for the brand's 20th anniversary. The name comes from an extra 300 days of aging.
notes: The maker lists the wrapper as Cameroon (Ecuador). It gives no strength word; its strength gauge reads 60 out of 100. Sizes come from a European retailer, which also shows a limited Gran Toro (6 x 58).
verifyNotes: Set officialName to null: the maker's own page is titled León Jimenes Series 300, so the given name is already right. Notes now give the maker's strength gauge (60 of 100).

about: The personal blend of La Aurora head Guillermo León, introduced in 2010 and also sold as Guillermo León Family Reserve. It is known for its double binder of Dominican and Cameroon leaf.

Also sold as Guillermo León Family Reserve.

about: A La Aurora line launched in 2012 to honor Fernando León, who ran the company from the 1950s until 2009. It is based on the personal blend once made only for him, his family and friends.
notes: Neptune rates it medium; the maker gives no strength word and its gauge reads 75 out of 100. The maker lists Dominican and Brazilian filler; halfwheel and Neptune add Peru. It is a rebrand of Fernando León's personal Don Fernando cigar. A limited box-pressed 6 x 54 was also made.
verifyNotes: Blend, sizes and 2012 launch confirmed. Notes now add the maker's strength gauge (75 of 100) beside Neptune's Medium, and drop the Cameroon remark, which halfwheel says applied only to the early personal blend.

about: A single-size limited lancero from La Aurora released in 2022 for what would have been Fernando León's 100th birthday. Its Dominican corojo wrapper comes from a La Aurora growing project in Bonao, first harvested in 2008.
notes: Limited to 1,000 boxes of 10. It is a separate cigar from the Fernando León Family Reserve and a different blend from the Fernando León Limited Edition. Strength is from the halfwheel review.
verifyNotes: All spec fields match halfwheel. Fixed about: halfwheel says the company started the Bonao corojo project shortly before his death, not that he started it. Removed the claim that the maker publishes no strength, which I could not check.

about: A limited belicoso from La Aurora released in 2021 in honor of Fernando León. Its corojo wrapper leaf was bought by León himself before he died in 2009 and sat unused until this project.
notes: halfwheel reports 150 boxes of 15. It lists the wrapper origin as undisclosed, while Neptune calls it Dominican-grown corojo. Neptune lists it as medium strength, but halfwheel's reviewer found it mild to barely medium. It is a different blend from the Fernando León Family Reserve.
verifyNotes: Blend, size, 2021 release and undisclosed wrapper origin confirmed. Strength Medium is Neptune's word; notes now add that halfwheel's reviewer found it mild to barely medium, which the researcher left out.
